title: Accessing Gapped Chiral Phase with Auxiliary-Assisted PEPS
abstract: It has been controversial whether infinite projected entangled pair state (PEPS) can faithfully describe chiral gapped phases in two dimensions or not. Finite-bond-dimension PEPS can capture many local and topological properties of chiral phases, but generically develop spurious long-range power-law like correlations. We introduce an auxiliary-assisted framework that bypass this obstruction by embedding the physical chiral system together with an auxiliary time-reversed partner, yielding a non-chiral enlarged representation whose physical chiral sector is recovered with controlled decoupling. For both a free-fermion Chern insulator and an interacting chiral spin liquid, the resulting PEPS show clean gapped correlation functions, and a finite transfer-matrix correlation length, in contrast with the artificial long-range tail of direct chiral PEPS representations. There exist small and negligibly coupling between the physical and auxiliary systems due to the finite entanglement effect, which only affect short-ranged local quantities. Despite the nonchiral enlarged representation, the chiral topological information remains encoded in the entanglement. Using layer-resolved momentum projection, we recover the expected universal chiral entanglement boundary spectrum. Our study provides a practical route to access gapped chiral phases with finite bond-dimension PEPS by changing the representation problem rather than directly studying the chiral pure state.
summary: The paper presents an auxiliary-assisted PEPS method to overcome the difficulty of simulating gapped chiral phases with finite bond dimensions. By coupling the physical system to its time-reversed partner, it eliminates artificial long-range correlations found in direct representations. This technique successfully validates the description of both fermionic and interacting chiral spin liquids while preserving key topological entanglement signatures.
main_problem: The primary challenge is representing gapped chiral phases using finite bond-dimension PEPS, as direct representations introduce spurious long-range power-law correlations inconsistent with true gapped behavior.
main_result: An auxiliary-assisted framework successfully bypasses this obstruction by embedding the physical system with a time-reversed partner, yielding clean short-range correlation functions for both free-fermion and interacting chiral models.
method: The authors introduce an auxiliary-assisted PEPS formalism where the physical state is enlarged to a non-chiral representation. Physical observables are recovered by tracing out the auxiliary degrees of freedom, allowing the use of standard tensor network techniques like CTMRG.
model_or_system: The study applies to gapped chiral phases, specifically modeling free-fermion Chern insulators and interacting chiral spin liquids (e.g., SU(2) spins on a square lattice). The method involves constructing an enlarged Hamiltonian by coupling the physical system with its time-reversed auxiliary counterpart.
key_observables: Clean exponential decay of correlation functions, finite transfer-matrix correlation length ($\xi$), and recovery of universal chiral entanglement boundary spectra via layer-resolved momentum projection.
important_parameters: Finite bond dimension ($D$), residual coupling strength ($\lambda_i$), and the topological nature of the underlying phase (e.g., SU(2)$_1$ chiral order).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that the small, residual couplings between the physical and auxiliary systems are weak enough to only affect short-range local quantities, thus preserving low-energy physics.
figures_summary: Figures compare energy convergence and long-distance correlations for direct vs. auxiliary PEPS setups, showing artifact removal in the latter. Other figures detail entanglement spectra analysis by projecting onto specific momentum sectors on a cylinder.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem of spurious correlations in chiral PEPS. It then introduces the auxiliary-assisted formalism and applies it to free-fermion and interacting spin models, demonstrating artifact removal via correlation function analysis. Finally, it uses entanglement spectrum analysis by fixing auxiliary momenta to confirm the recovery of universal chiral topological information.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, practical computational tool (auxiliary embedding) to study highly constrained quantum phases like chiral magnets and superconductors using established tensor network methods, which is crucial for understanding exotic condensed matter states.
